observed_reality: Fixed capability plan requires low-latency Clay data transformation plus visual/image/video and audio transport.
Python buffer/memoryview is a plausible reference-implementation substrate for low-copy transport, but host behavior is not Clay semantic authority.
grf.generated_hypothesis: A readonly memoryview can serve as a provenance-stable zero-copy Clay ingress buffer even when the producer originally owns mutable storage.
grf.counter_reality: Readonly only removes mutation authority from the view consumer; the producer can still mutate the backing storage and invalidate a previously bound provenance digest.
grf.falsifier: Create one readonly memoryview over bytearray, hash/read it, mutate the producer bytearray once, then re-read/re-hash the readonly view.

external_primary_evidence.finding: The official example shows a readonly memoryview reflecting mutations made through the original writable view/backing bytearray.

external_primary_evidence.source: Python 3.14 C API Buffer Protocol documentation
external_primary_evidence.finding: The buffer protocol is explicitly an access view onto an underlying exporter and supports direct/zero-copy access; readonly describes consumer write access, not a snapshot guarantee.

exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment.name: READONLY_MEMORYVIEW_PROVENANCE_MUTATION
exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment.result: Producer mutation changed bytes and digest despite readonly view; readonly is not provenance immutability.

deterministic_candidate_test.scope: local sandbox reference prototype only; NOT product-repository code and NOT Clay Machine PASS
deterministic_candidate_test.candidate_contract: ClayIOEnvelope/v1 with explicit DATA/VISUAL/AUDIO plane, provenance/timestamps/format identity, immutable-buffer digest, zero-copy only for C-contiguous memoryview ultimately backed by built-in immutable bytes; mutable/unknown exporters are snapshotted.
covered: readonly view over mutable exporter snapshot

ordinary_micro_measurements.warning: Sandbox microbenchmarks only; no release performance claim.
ordinary_micro_measurements.interpretation: In this prototype the mandatory full-buffer SHA-256 dominates 1 MiB ingress cost; copying mutable input added far less cost than hashing. This does not justify always-copy or always-hash production policy; streaming/incremental provenance remains open.

architecture_delta.rule: Do not equate readonly buffer access with immutable provenance. Until Clay selects and tests explicit buffer lifetime/lease/epoch semantics, zero-copy provenance-bound ingress should be restricted to storage proven immutable for the admitted implementation; mutable or semantically unknown exporters require snapshot/copy or fail closed.
non_claims: No canonical Clay Bytes/Buffer language type selected.
No VM instruction or compiler lowering added.
No product code committed from this experiment.
architecture_delta.next_falsifier: Define the smallest canonical Clay Buffer/Bytes ownership + lifetime contract at the typed/effect boundary, then compare immutable-owned, copied-mutable, and explicit leased/epoch-checked borrowed buffers through one VM ingress path with provenance and latency measurements.
